category: relay/P2P — SIGNALLING with encrypted fallback transport

free_tier.stated: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.

egress.terms: Free public relays, rate-limited. Self-hosting a relay is free and unlimited (open licence) — the cost moves to your own bandwidth.

interface_detail: QUIC over TLS 1.3; Rust crate `iroh`, bindings for other languages
tooling: `iroh` crate; relay is a library, not a service with an upload endpoint
chaining: This is SIGNALLING, not relaying, in the normal case: 'roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'. The relay carries bytes only when hole punching fails, which is what makes the free tier viable at all.
limits_note: Not a storage provider. Only relayed bytes hit the operator, hence the per-connection rate limit rather than a byte quota.
reliability_note: 'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed' and 'Do not rely on it for production workloads' — the free tier is explicitly capacity-unstable by design.

evidence.proved: 'In practice, roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'; relays are stateless and cannot read traffic (QUIC/TLS 1.3)
'The exact rate limits aren't published today, as they get tuned as needed ... applied per connection'; 'Do not rely on it for production workloads'
Free: 'Rate limited' / 'Variable'; Pro $19/mo: 10,000 connections, shared relays, 5 MB/s; Dedicated $199/mo/region: unlimited
'100 GB of relay egress per month, then $0.09/GB'; 'A 5 MB/s rate limit'
worked example: 2,000 users x 10 GB/mo; 'if 98% of the traffic could travel directly ... only the remaining 2% (400 GB) would pass through'

notes: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.
